source.text: Τὰ τέκνα, ὑπακούετε τοῖς γονεῦσιν ὑμῶν ἐν κυρίῳ, τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν δίκαιον·

records.literal_gloss: The children, obey the parents of you in [the] Lord, this for is right;

en.L: Children, obey your parents in [the] Lord, for this is right.
en.B: Children, obey your parents in the Lord, because this is right.
en.R: Children, obey your parents as people who belong to the Lord. This is the right thing to do.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "in the Lord" is part of the text
alternatives: omit "in the Lord": "Children, obey your parents, for this is right"
decisions.reason: A few early manuscripts, among them Codex Vaticanus and some Western witnesses, lack the words ἐν κυρίῳ. Most manuscripts have them, and the same phrase runs through these household instructions (5:22; 6:5, 6:7). Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: in the Lord goes with "obey": obey as those who belong to the Lord
alternatives: "your parents who are in the Lord": only parents who are believers
decisions.reason: The phrase says how and why the children obey, not which parents are meant. In Colossians 3:20 the same command ends "for this is pleasing in the Lord".

decisions.choice: right: what is just, as God's own law shows
decisions.reason: δίκαιον is what is just and fitting. Verse 2 at once grounds it in the commandment to honor father and mother.

decisions.choice: children: members of the congregation, addressed directly
decisions.reason: Letters were read aloud to the gathered church (Colossians 4:16). Paul speaks to the children themselves, as he does to wives, husbands, fathers, slaves and masters, as members of the body of Christ.

decisions.choice: as people who belong to the Lord
decisions.reason: Readable says what "in the Lord" means here (m2).

source.text: τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα, ἥτις ἐστὶν ἐντολὴ πρώτη ἐν ἐπαγγελίᾳ, ἵνα εὖ σοι γένηται καὶ ἔσῃ μακροχρόνιος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.

records.literal_gloss: Honor the father of you and the mother, which is [the] commandment first with promise, \v 3 that well to you it may be and you will be long-lived upon the earth.

en.L: "Honor your father and mother," which is [the] first commandment with a promise, \v 3 "so that it may be well with you, and you will be long-lived on the earth."
en.B: "Honor your father and mother." This is the first commandment that comes with a promise: \v 3 "so that things may go well for you and you may enjoy a long life on the earth."
en.R: God's law says, "Honor your father and mother." This is the first of God's commands that comes with a promise. \v 3 The promise is, "Then things will go well for you, and you will live a long time on the earth."

decisions.choice: a quotation of the fifth commandment, Exodus 20:12 and Deuteronomy 5:16
decisions.reason: Paul quotes the commandment as the Greek Old Testament has it, with changes. He leaves out the end, "in the land that the LORD your God is giving you", and he adds a note of his own between the command and the promise. "That it may go well with you" is in Deuteronomy 5:16 (and in the Greek of Exodus 20:12), not in the Hebrew of Exodus 20:12. The last verb is future, ἔσῃ, "you will be".

decisions.choice: the first commandment with a promise: the first of the Ten Commandments to have a promise attached
alternatives: a commandment of first importance, with a promise
decisions.reason: The earlier commandments carry no promise made to the one who keeps them; this one promises long life. Exodus 20:6 speaks of God's steadfast love to those who keep his commands, but as a description of God, not a promise attached to one command.

decisions.choice: the earth: the promise now reaches readers wherever they live
decisions.reason: In Exodus and Deuteronomy the promise is long life in the land God was giving Israel. Without the words about that land, γῆς can mean the earth at large, which suits readers in Asia Minor. The same word can also mean "land".

decisions.choice: it may be well with you: that you may prosper and do well
decisions.reason: εὖ σοι γένηται is a common phrase for things going well in life.

decisions.choice: quotation marks around the commandment; Paul's note left outside them
decisions.reason: The words of the commandment are marked as a quotation (m1), so that the reader can tell them from Paul's comment on them.

decisions.choice: God's law says; The promise is
decisions.reason: Readable says where the words come from and that verse 3 is the promise (m1, m2).

source.text: Καὶ οἱ πατέρες, μὴ παροργίζετε τὰ τέκνα ὑμῶν, ἀλλὰ ἐκτρέφετε αὐτὰ ἐν παιδείᾳ καὶ νουθεσίᾳ κυρίου.

records.literal_gloss: And the fathers, not provoke-to-anger the children of you, but bring up them in training and admonition of [the] Lord.

en.L: And fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, but rear them in [the] training and admonition of [the] Lord.
en.B: Fathers, do not drive your children to anger. Instead, bring them up with the Lord's training and correction.
en.R: Fathers, do not treat your children in ways that make them angry. Instead, as you raise them, train them and correct them in the way the Lord teaches.

decisions.choice: fathers: the head of the household, who had authority over the children
decisions.reason: Verse 1 speaks of both parents; now Paul addresses the fathers, who in Roman law and custom held great power over their children. He limits that power: it is not to be used to crush them. The plural can mean "parents" (Hebrews 11:23), but here Paul has just used another word for parents.

decisions.choice: provoke to anger: to make children resentful by harsh or unfair treatment
decisions.reason: Colossians 3:21 gives the reason in its parallel: "so that they do not lose heart". Paul forbade anger that festers in 4:26 and 4:31; fathers must not cause it in their children.

decisions.choice: training and admonition: upbringing that includes discipline, and correction by word
alternatives: discipline and instruction (narrower: punishment and teaching)
decisions.reason: παιδείᾳ is the whole training of a child, including discipline (Hebrews 12:5-11). νουθεσίᾳ is setting someone right by words of warning and instruction (1 Corinthians 10:11).

decisions.choice: of the Lord: the training the Lord himself gives, through the fathers
decisions.reason: The genitive most likely means the training belongs to the Lord and comes from him: fathers bring up their children as the Lord would.

decisions.choice: training and correction
decisions.reason: The English words cover both parts of each Greek word (m3); "discipline" alone can suggest only punishment.

decisions.choice: in the way the Lord teaches
decisions.reason: Readable spells out "of the Lord" (m4).

source.text: Οἱ δοῦλοι, ὑπακούετε τοῖς κατὰ σάρκα κυρίοις μετὰ φόβου καὶ τρόμου ἐν ἁπλότητι τῆς καρδίας ὑμῶν ὡς τῷ Χριστῷ, μὴ κατ’ ὀφθαλμοδουλίαν ὡς ἀνθρωπάρεσκοι ἀλλ’ ὡς δοῦλοι Χριστοῦ ποιοῦντες τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ, ἐκ ψυχῆς μετ’ εὐνοίας δουλεύοντες, ὡς τῷ κυρίῳ καὶ οὐκ ἀνθρώποις, εἰδότες ὅτι ἕκαστος, ὃ ἂν ποιήσῃ ἀγαθόν, τοῦτο κομίσεται παρὰ κυρίου, εἴτε δοῦλος εἴτε ἐλεύθερος.

records.literal_gloss: The slaves, obey the according to flesh masters with fear and trembling in sincerity of the heart of you as to the Christ, \v 6 not by way of eye-service as people-pleasers but as slaves of Christ doing the will of the God, from [the] soul, \v 7 with goodwill serving-as-slaves, as to the Lord and not to men, \v 8 knowing that each, whatever he may do good, this he will receive back from [the] Lord, whether slave or free.

en.L: Slaves, obey [your] masters according to the flesh with fear and trembling, in sincerity of your heart, as to the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, \v 6 not by way of eye-service, as {{gender:people-pleasers|men-pleasers}}, but as slaves of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, doing the will of God, from the soul \v 7 serving as slaves with goodwill, as to the Lord and not to {{gender:people|men}}, \v 8 knowing that each one will receive back from [the] Lord whatever good [each] does, whether slave or free.
en.B: Slaves, obey your earthly masters with fear and trembling and with an undivided heart, as you obey {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. \v 6 Do not work only while they are watching, to win their favor. Work as slaves of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, who do the will of God. Serve as slaves with all your heart \v 7 and with goodwill, as serving the Lord and not people, \v 8 because you know that the Lord will repay each one for whatever good they do, whether they are slave or free.
en.R: Slaves, obey your masters here on earth with deep respect and great care. Obey them with an honest heart, just as you obey {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. \v 6 Do not work hard only when they are watching you, just to make them like you. You are slaves of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, so do what God wants. Serve with all your heart, \v 7 and be glad to do it. Serve as if you were working for the Lord and not for people. \v 8 You know that the Lord will reward everyone for the good they do, whether they are slaves or free.

decisions.choice: slaves in the Roman world
decisions.reason: Slaves made up a large part of many households in a city like Ephesus. They were legally their owners' property, though many were later freed. Slaves and masters belonged to the same churches (verse 9; Colossians 3:22-4:1; Philemon 10-16). The letter does not discuss whether slavery should exist; it speaks to people inside it and puts slaves and masters under one Lord (verse 9).

decisions.choice: masters according to the flesh, and the Lord: earthly owners, and Christ, their real Lord
decisions.reason: The same word, κύριος, means both "master" and "Lord". The owners are masters only κατὰ σάρκα, in this life; the Lord whom slaves really serve, and who repays them, is Christ (as in Colossians 3:22-24).

decisions.choice: fear and trembling: deep respect and earnest care, not terror
decisions.reason: Paul uses the same pair of words for his own coming to Corinth (1 Corinthians 2:3), for the Corinthians' welcome of Titus (2 Corinthians 7:15) and for working out salvation (Philippians 2:12). The respect is owed finally to Christ: "as to Christ".

decisions.choice: eye-service: working only when watched, to please people
decisions.reason: ὀφθαλμοδουλίαν is service done for the master's eye (also Colossians 3:22). ἀνθρωπάρεσκοι are those who aim only to please people.

decisions.choice: from the soul goes with "serving": serving wholeheartedly
alternatives: "doing the will of God from the soul"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts a comma after "the will of God", so "from the soul" begins the next phrase and describes the serving. "From the soul" means with one's whole self (Colossians 3:23).

decisions.choice: goodwill: willing, glad service
decisions.reason: εὐνοίας is a kind and willing attitude: slaves serve not grudgingly but gladly, because the Lord is the one they serve.

decisions.choice: the Lord repays every good deed, and a person's rank makes no difference
decisions.reason: Slaves could expect no reward from their owners, but the Lord will repay them; the same rule holds for the free, including the masters of verse 9 (Colossians 3:24-25; 2 Corinthians 5:10).

decisions.choice: masters (the owners); the Lord (Christ)
decisions.reason: One Greek word, two English ones (m2), so that the contrast shows, as in Colossians 3:22.

decisions.choice: slaves; serve as slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, never "servant". Balanced keeps the verb's sense with "serve as slaves"; Readable says "you are slaves of Christ" and then "serve".

decisions.choice: {{gender:people-pleasers|men-pleasers}}; {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The words mean human beings in general; "men" is the traditional form.

decisions.choice: with deep respect and great care
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m3); Literal and Balanced keep "fear and trembling".

decisions.choice: with all your heart
decisions.reason: The English idiom for wholehearted effort; Literal keeps "from the soul" (m5).

decisions.choice: each one ... [each] (L); they (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek uses a masculine singular for "each" in a general sense; the levels avoid a gendered pronoun.

source.text: Καὶ οἱ κύριοι, τὰ αὐτὰ ποιεῖτε πρὸς αὐτούς, ἀνιέντες τὴν ἀπειλήν, εἰδότες ὅτι καὶ αὐτῶν καὶ ὑμῶν ὁ κύριός ἐστιν ἐν οὐρανοῖς, καὶ προσωπολημψία οὐκ ἔστιν παρ’ αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And the masters, the same things do toward them, giving up the threatening, knowing that both of them and of you the Master is in heavens, and partiality not is with him.

en.L: And masters, do the same things toward them, giving up threatening, knowing that both their Master and yours is in [the] heavens, and there is no partiality with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Masters, treat your slaves in the same way. Stop threatening them, because you know that the one who is both their Master and yours is in heaven, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not show favoritism.
en.R: Masters, treat your slaves in the same good way. Do not threaten them. Remember that you and your slaves have the same Master, the Lord in heaven. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} treats everyone the same.

decisions.choice: the same things: act toward slaves in the same spirit, as serving the Lord
alternatives: do good to them, as the Lord repays good (verse 8)
decisions.reason: Masters are not told to obey their slaves. They are to bring the same sincerity and goodwill to their part, knowing that the Lord sees them too (verses 5-8).

decisions.choice: giving up the threatening: dropping the threats used to control slaves
decisions.reason: Masters kept slaves in line by threats of beating, or of selling them and so parting them from their families. ἀνιέντες means to let go of something; the article points to the threats masters customarily used.

decisions.choice: masters, and the Master in heaven: Christ, the Lord of masters and slaves alike
decisions.reason: The same word names the masters and their Master. Masters are answerable to the same Lord as their slaves (Colossians 4:1).

decisions.choice: partiality: favoring someone because of who they are
decisions.reason: προσωπολημψία comes from a Hebrew idiom, "to lift the face", meaning to favor a person (Deuteronomy 10:17; Romans 2:11; Colossians 3:25). The Lord does not judge by rank.

decisions.choice: masters; Master
decisions.reason: "Masters" for the owners and "Master" with a capital for Christ, keeping the play on one Greek word (m3), as in Colossians 4:1. Readable adds "the Lord" so the reader knows who is meant.

decisions.choice: your slaves
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "them" are.

source.text: Τοῦ λοιποῦ ἐνδυναμοῦσθε ἐν κυρίῳ καὶ ἐν τῷ κράτει τῆς ἰσχύος αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: For the rest, be strengthened in [the] Lord and in the might of the strength of him.

en.L: Finally, be made strong in [the] Lord and in the might of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} strength.
en.B: Finally, be made strong in the Lord and in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mighty strength.
en.R: Finally, let the Lord make you strong. Your strength comes from being joined to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "finally" with no address
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "Finally, my brothers", with a slightly different form of the opening word. The SBLGNT follows early manuscripts that lack "my brothers". Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: finally: turning to the last part of the letter
decisions.reason: Τοῦ λοιποῦ can also mean "from now on" (Galatians 6:17). Here it introduces the closing section, as the similar phrase does in Philippians 3:1 and 4:8.

decisions.choice: be strengthened: a strength that comes from the Lord
decisions.reason: ἐνδυναμοῦσθε is passive: believers are made strong by the Lord, in union with him, not by their own effort.

decisions.choice: the might of his strength: his overwhelming power
decisions.reason: The two words for power are piled together, as in 1:19, where they describe the power God used to raise Christ from the dead (1:19-20). The same power is at work in believers.

decisions.choice: let the Lord make you strong; being joined to him
decisions.reason: Readable says who gives the strength (m3) and what "in the Lord" means.

source.text: ἐνδύσασθε τὴν πανοπλίαν τοῦ θεοῦ πρὸς τὸ δύνασθαι ὑμᾶς στῆναι πρὸς τὰς μεθοδείας τοῦ διαβόλου·

records.literal_gloss: Put on the full armor of the God toward the to be able you to stand against the schemes of the devil;

en.L: Put on the full armor of God, so as to be able to stand against the stratagems of the devil.
en.B: Clothe yourselves in God's complete armor, so that you can hold your ground against the devil's cunning plans.
en.R: Put on all the armor that God gives you. Then you will be able to stand firm when the devil tries to trick you.

decisions.choice: full armor: the complete equipment of a heavily armed soldier
decisions.reason: πανοπλίαν is the full set of weapons and armor. Roman soldiers were a familiar sight, and Paul writes as a prisoner guarded by them (verse 20; Acts 28:16).

decisions.choice: the armor of God: armor God provides, and his own
decisions.reason: God gives it to his people, and it is the armor God himself wears in Isaiah 59:17 (see verses 14-17).

decisions.choice: stand: hold one's position against attack
decisions.reason: The verb is used of soldiers standing their ground; it comes again in verses 13 and 14. Believers are not told to win new ground but to stand firm in what Christ has already won (1:20-22).

decisions.choice: schemes: cunning methods of deceit
decisions.reason: μεθοδείας is the word used in 4:14 of the scheming of deceitful teachers. The devil attacks by trickery more than by open force.

decisions.choice: hold your ground (B); stand firm (R)
decisions.reason: The English idioms bring out the military sense (m3).

decisions.choice: the armor that God gives you
decisions.reason: Readable says that the armor comes from God (m2).

source.text: ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν ἡμῖν ἡ πάλη πρὸς αἷμα καὶ σάρκα, ἀλλὰ πρὸς τὰς ἀρχάς, πρὸς τὰς ἐξουσίας, πρὸς τοὺς κοσμοκράτορας τοῦ σκότους τούτου, πρὸς τὰ πνευματικὰ τῆς πονηρίας ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις.

records.literal_gloss: Because not is to us the wrestling against blood and flesh, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the world-rulers of the darkness this, against the spiritual [forces] of the evil in the heavenly [places].

en.L: For our wrestling is not against blood and flesh, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the world-rulers of this darkness, against the spiritual [forces] of evil in the heavenly [places].
en.B: Our fight is not with flesh and blood. It is with the rulers, with the authorities, with the world rulers of this darkness, with the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly places.
en.R: We are not fighting against human beings. We are fighting against the rulers and the authorities, against the powers that rule over the world's darkness, against the evil spiritual forces in the spiritual world.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "our" wrestling
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts, among them P46 and Codex Vaticanus, read "your" in place of ἡμῖν, "to us". The two words differ by one letter in Greek and were often confused. Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: wrestling: close, hand-to-hand struggle
decisions.reason: πάλη is the word for a wrestling match. Paul mixes the picture of wrestling with that of armor: the fight is at close quarters.

decisions.choice: blood and flesh: human beings
decisions.reason: The phrase means mortal human beings (Galatians 1:16; Hebrews 2:14, which has the same order). The enemy is not other people.

decisions.choice: the rulers and the authorities: spiritual powers opposed to God
decisions.reason: The same pair of words is used in 1:21 and 3:10 of powers in the heavenly realm, over which Christ now reigns (1:21; Colossians 2:15).

decisions.choice: world-rulers of this darkness: powers that hold the present dark world in their grip
decisions.reason: κοσμοκράτωρ is found only here in the New Testament. It was used of beings or rulers thought to rule the whole world. "This darkness" is the world as it is now, set against the light (5:8, 5:11; Colossians 1:13).

decisions.choice: the spiritual forces of evil: evil spiritual beings
decisions.reason: The neuter plural adjective πνευματικὰ means "spiritual [beings or forces]"; "of evil" says what they are like.

decisions.choice: in the heavenly places: the unseen realm
decisions.reason: The phrase is the one used in 1:3, 1:20, 2:6 and 3:10. It is the unseen world where Christ reigns and believers already share his place, and where hostile powers are still at work (3:10). It does not mean that evil dwells with God.

decisions.choice: flesh and blood (B); human beings (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the English idiom, in the order English uses; Readable says what it means (m3). Literal keeps the Greek order, "blood and flesh".

decisions.choice: in the spiritual world
decisions.reason: In plain English "in heaven" would suggest that these evil forces live where God is. Readable names the unseen realm instead (m7).

decisions.choice: fight; fighting
decisions.reason: Wrestling is a sport in English; the point is a real struggle (m2).

source.text: διὰ τοῦτο ἀναλάβετε τὴν πανοπλίαν τοῦ θεοῦ, ἵνα δυνηθῆτε ἀντιστῆναι ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ πονηρᾷ καὶ ἅπαντα κατεργασάμενοι στῆναι.

records.literal_gloss: Because of this take up the full armor of the God, that you may be able to withstand in the day the evil and all things having done to stand.

en.L: For this reason, take up the full armor of God, so that you may be able to resist on the evil day and, having accomplished all things, to stand.
en.B: For this reason, take up God's complete armor. Then you will be able to resist on the evil day and, having carried everything through, remain standing.
en.R: So pick up all the armor God gives you. Then, when the day of evil comes, you will be able to resist the enemy. And after you have done all you can, you will still be standing strong.

decisions.choice: the evil day: a time of fierce attack by the devil, which may come at any time
alternatives: the final day of trouble before Christ returns
decisions.reason: Paul has said that "the days are evil" (5:16). The evil day is most likely any time when the attack is at its worst. Others take it as the time of great trouble before the end.

decisions.choice: having done everything: having made every preparation and carried the fight through
decisions.reason: κατεργασάμενοι usually means to do or to bring something about; it can also mean to overcome. Either way, at the end of the battle the believer is still standing.

decisions.choice: take up: pick up armor and weapons for battle
decisions.reason: ἀναλάβετε is used of taking up arms; verse 16 uses the same verb for the shield.

decisions.choice: resist the enemy
decisions.reason: Readable says whom they resist (verses 11-12).

source.text: στῆτε οὖν περιζωσάμενοι τὴν ὀσφὺν ὑμῶν ἐν ἀληθείᾳ, καὶ ἐνδυσάμενοι τὸν θώρακα τῆς δικαιοσύνης, καὶ ὑποδησάμενοι τοὺς πόδας ἐν ἑτοιμασίᾳ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου τῆς εἰρήνης, ἐν πᾶσιν ἀναλαβόντες τὸν θυρεὸν τῆς πίστεως, ἐν ᾧ δυνήσεσθε πάντα τὰ βέλη τοῦ πονηροῦ πεπυρωμένα σβέσαι·

records.literal_gloss: Stand therefore having girded the waist of you with truth, and having put on the breastplate of the righteousness, \v 15 and having shod the feet in readiness of the gospel of the peace, \v 16 in all having taken up the shield of the faith, with which you will be able all the arrows of the evil [one] having been set on fire to quench;

en.L: Stand, then, having girded your waist with truth, and having put on the breastplate of righteousness, \v 15 and having shod [your] feet with the readiness of the gospel of peace, \v 16 in all [things] having taken up the shield of faith, by which you will be able to quench all the burning arrows of the evil [one].
en.B: So stand your ground. Tie truth around your waist as a belt, and put on righteousness as your breastplate. \v 15 For shoes, put on the readiness that the gospel of peace gives. \v 16 In every situation take up faith as your shield; with it you will be able to put out all the burning arrows of the evil one.
en.R: So stand firm! Put on truth like a belt around your waist. Put on righteousness like a soldier's breastplate to protect your chest. \v 15 Let the good news of peace make you ready, like shoes on your feet. \v 16 At all times, hold up faith like a shield. With it you can put out all the burning arrows that the evil one shoots at you.

decisions.choice: the belt and the breastplate are God's own armor in Isaiah
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 11:5 righteousness and faithfulness are the belt of the coming king from David's line. In Isaiah 59:17 God puts on righteousness as a breastplate and salvation as a helmet (see verse 17). The armor God and his Messiah wear is now given to his people.

decisions.choice: a soldier's equipment
decisions.reason: To gird the waist was to tie up a long tunic with a belt, ready for action. The breastplate covered the chest. Soldiers wore strong sandals or boots for marching and footing. θυρεὸν is the large oblong shield, shaped like a door, that covered the whole body. Arrows wrapped in burning pitch were used in ancient warfare to set things alight.

decisions.choice: the participles describe what is done in order to stand
decisions.reason: The one command is στῆτε, "stand". The participles ("having girded", "having put on", "having shod", "having taken up") describe the arming that goes with standing firm.

decisions.choice: truth and righteousness: the truth and righteousness God gives, lived out
decisions.reason: In this letter truth is the truth of the gospel (1:13; 4:21) and also truthful living (4:15, 4:25); righteousness is the new life created by God (4:24; 5:9), and in Isaiah 59:17 it is God's own. The words cover both what God gives and how believers live; every level keeps "truth" and "righteousness".

decisions.choice: the readiness that the gospel of peace gives
alternatives: readiness to proclaim the gospel of peace
the firm footing of the gospel
decisions.reason: ἑτοιμασίᾳ means readiness or preparation. It most likely names the steady readiness for battle that comes from the gospel, which brings peace with God and between people (2:14-17). The feet recall Isaiah 52:7, "how beautiful are the feet of the one who brings good news, who announces peace", so the readiness may instead be readiness to announce the gospel (compare verses 19-20).

decisions.choice: the feet and the gospel of peace recall Isaiah 52:7
decisions.reason: Isaiah 52:7 speaks of the feet of the messenger who brings good news of peace; Paul echoed the same chapter's "peace" in 2:17.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "in all [things]"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "above all" or "besides all" (a different preposition). With the SBLGNT reading, ἐν πᾶσιν means "in every situation" or possibly "with all these". Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: the evil one: the devil
decisions.reason: The article and singular point to a person: the devil of verse 11.

decisions.choice: the participles become commands
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn each piece of armor into a command of its own after "stand" (m3), which reads naturally in English.

decisions.choice: truth as a belt; righteousness as a breastplate; faith as a shield
decisions.reason: "Belt of truth" and the like mean that truth is the belt; Balanced and Readable say so plainly. Literal keeps the Greek wording.

decisions.choice: to protect your chest; that the evil one shoots at you
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the breastplate and the arrows are (m2).

decisions.choice: put out
decisions.reason: Plain English for extinguishing a fire; Literal says "quench".

source.text: καὶ τὴν περικεφαλαίαν τοῦ σωτηρίου δέξασθε, καὶ τὴν μάχαιραν τοῦ πνεύματος, ὅ ἐστιν ῥῆμα θεοῦ, διὰ πάσης προσευχῆς καὶ δεήσεως, προσευχόμενοι ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ ἐν πνεύματι, καὶ εἰς αὐτὸ ἀγρυπνοῦντες ἐν πάσῃ προσκαρτερήσει καὶ δεήσει περὶ πάντων τῶν ἁγίων, καὶ ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ, ἵνα μοι δοθῇ λόγος ἐν ἀνοίξει τοῦ στόματός μου, ἐν παρρησίᾳ γνωρίσαι τὸ μυστήριον τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ὑπὲρ οὗ πρεσβεύω ἐν ἁλύσει, ἵνα ἐν αὐτῷ παρρησιάσωμαι ὡς δεῖ με λαλῆσαι.

records.literal_gloss: And the helmet of the salvation receive, and the sword of the Spirit, which is [the] word of God, \v 18 through all prayer and petition, praying at every time in [the] Spirit, and to it keeping alert in all perseverance and petition concerning all the holy [ones], \v 19 and for me, that to me may be given a word in [the] opening of the mouth of me, in boldness to make known the mystery of the gospel, \v 20 for which I am an ambassador in a chain, that in it I may speak boldly as it is necessary [for] me to speak.

en.L: And receive the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is [the] word of God, \v 18 through all prayer and petition praying at every time in [the] Spirit, and to this [end] keeping alert with all perseverance and petition for all the holy [ones], \v 19 and for me, that a word may be given to me in the opening of my mouth, to make known with boldness the mystery of the gospel, \v 20 for which I am an ambassador in a chain, that in it I may speak boldly, as I must speak.
en.B: Receive salvation as your helmet, and the sword that the Spirit gives, which is the word of God. \v 18 Pray in the Spirit at every opportunity, with every kind of prayer and request. To that end, keep watch, never giving up, and make requests for all God's holy people. \v 19 Pray also for me, that when I open my mouth I will be given the words to make known with boldness the mystery of the gospel. \v 20 For its sake I am an ambassador, though in a chain. Pray that I may speak of it boldly, as I must.
en.R: Accept salvation as your helmet. Take the word of God as your sword, the sword the Spirit gives you. \v 18 Pray at all times with the help of the Spirit. Pray in every way, and bring all your requests to God. So stay awake, keep on praying, and do not give up. Pray for all of God's people. \v 19 Pray for me too. Ask God to give me the right words whenever I speak, so that I can boldly tell people the mystery of the good news. It is God's plan, once hidden but now made known. \v 20 I am an ambassador sent to announce this good news, even though I am a prisoner in chains. Pray that I will speak about it boldly, as I should.

decisions.choice: the helmet and the sword come from Isaiah
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 59:17 God wears "the helmet of salvation". In Isaiah 11:4 the coming king strikes the earth with the rod of his mouth, and in Isaiah 49:2 the Lord's servant says God made his mouth like a sharp sword. The sword here is a word that is spoken.

decisions.choice: receive: a new command; the helmet and sword are received from God
decisions.reason: After the participles of verses 14-16, δέξασθε is a command again. It means to take what is offered: these are gifts, not things believers make for themselves.

decisions.choice: the sword is the word of God, and the Spirit gives it
alternatives: the Spirit is the word of God
decisions.reason: The sword belongs to the Spirit, who gives it and makes it effective. ῥῆμα is a word spoken, here God's message, the gospel (5:26; Romans 10:8, 10:17). The relative word ὅ is neuter, but it explains the whole phrase: the sword is God's word.

decisions.choice: praying and keeping alert go with the commands to stand and take the armor
decisions.reason: Verse 18 continues the same sentence with participles. Prayer is not one more piece of armor but the way the whole armor is worn.

decisions.choice: in the Spirit: by the help and leading of God's Spirit
alternatives: in your own spirit: with sincerity
decisions.reason: Access to the Father is "in one Spirit" (2:18); the Spirit helps believers pray (Romans 8:26; Jude 20).

decisions.choice: keeping alert: staying awake like a sentry
decisions.reason: ἀγρυπνοῦντες is to keep awake and watchful (Mark 13:33; Colossians 4:2 has a similar word): prayer is the watch kept in a long fight.

decisions.choice: a word given in the opening of my mouth: the right words whenever I speak
decisions.reason: To open one's mouth is a biblical way of saying to begin to speak (Psalm 51:15; Matthew 5:2). Paul asks that God would give him what to say.

decisions.choice: the mystery: God's plan, once hidden, now made known
decisions.reason: In 3:3-6 the mystery is that through the gospel Gentiles share with Jews in the promise in Christ.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the mystery of the gospel"
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts, among them Codex Vaticanus, read only "the mystery". Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: an ambassador in a chain
decisions.reason: An ambassador spoke with the authority of the ruler who sent him and was normally protected from harm. Paul, Christ's envoy, is held in custody, chained to a soldier (Acts 28:16, 28:20). The singular "chain" may be the chain that bound him to his guard.

decisions.choice: the sentence is divided; prayer becomes a command
decisions.reason: The Greek runs on from verse 17 to verse 20. Balanced and Readable divide it and turn the participles into commands, "Pray" (m4), and repeat "pray" in verses 19 and 20 so that it is clear what Paul asks.

decisions.choice: receive (L, B); accept (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to take what is offered (m2).

decisions.choice: God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: The holy ones are believers, set apart for God, as across Ephesians.

decisions.choice: It is God's plan, once hidden but now made known
decisions.reason: Readable explains "mystery" (m8).

decisions.choice: with the help of the Spirit
decisions.reason: Readable says what "in the Spirit" means (m5).

decisions.choice: sent to announce this good news
decisions.reason: Readable says what an ambassador does (m10).

source.text: Ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε καὶ ὑμεῖς τὰ κατ’ ἐμέ, τί πράσσω, πάντα γνωρίσει ὑμῖν Τυχικὸς ὁ ἀγαπητὸς ἀδελφὸς καὶ πιστὸς διάκονος ἐν κυρίῳ, ὃν ἔπεμψα πρὸς ὑμᾶς εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο ἵνα γνῶτε τὰ περὶ ἡμῶν καὶ παρακαλέσῃ τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: That and may know also you the things concerning me, what I am doing, all things will make known to you Tychicus the beloved brother and faithful servant in [the] Lord, \v 22 whom I sent to you for this very [thing], that you may know the things concerning us and he may encourage the hearts of you.

en.L: So that you also may know my affairs, how I am doing, Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful servant in [the] Lord, will make all things known to you. \v 22 I have sent him to you for this very purpose, that you may know the things concerning us and that he may encourage your hearts.
en.B: Tychicus, our dear brother and a faithful servant in the Lord, will tell you everything, so that you too may know how I am and what I am doing. \v 22 I am sending him to you for this very reason, so that you may know how we are and so that he may encourage your hearts.
en.R: Tychicus is a brother we love, and he serves the Lord faithfully. He will tell you all about how I am and what I am doing, so that you will know too. \v 22 That is why I am sending him to you. I want you to know how we are, and I want him to encourage you.

decisions.choice: Tychicus: one of Paul's companions from the province of Asia, who carried the letter
decisions.reason: Tychicus was from Asia (Acts 20:4); Paul later sent him to Ephesus (2 Timothy 4:12; Titus 3:12). Verses 21-22 match Colossians 4:7-8 almost word for word, so the two letters were most likely carried together.

decisions.choice: you too: as well as others receiving the same news
decisions.reason: καὶ ὑμεῖς most likely means that these readers, like others, will hear Paul's news; Colossians 4:7-9 makes the same promise to the church in Colossae.

decisions.choice: servant: one who serves the Lord in the work of the gospel
decisions.reason: διάκονος is the word Paul uses of himself in 3:7. Colossians 4:7 adds "fellow slave"; this verse does not.

decisions.choice: I have sent: the past tense of letters
decisions.reason: ἔπεμψα is past, written from the time the letter will be read, though Tychicus carries it.

decisions.choice: I am sending
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the tense natural in English (m4), as in Colossians 4:8.

decisions.choice: Tychicus is named first
decisions.reason: The Greek begins with the purpose clause and names Tychicus late. Balanced and Readable introduce him first so the sentence is easy to follow.

source.text: Εἰρήνη τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς καὶ ἀγάπη μετὰ πίστεως ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Peace to the brothers and love with faith from God [the] Father and [the] Lord Jesus Christ.

en.L: Peace to the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, and love with faith, from God [the] Father and [the] Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: Peace to the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, and love with faith, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: May God the Father and the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} give peace to the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, and love together with faith.

decisions.choice: the brothers: all the believers, men and women
decisions.reason: ἀδελφοῖς is used of the whole family of believers, as the letter's "you" includes everyone (5:22-6:9).

decisions.choice: love with faith: love given along with the faith they already have
alternatives: love and faith, both wished for them
decisions.reason: Paul wishes them love, joined to faith. Earlier he gave thanks for their faith and love (1:15).

decisions.choice: one source: God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: One preposition, ἀπὸ, governs both names, as in the greeting (1:2): the blessings come from the Father and Christ together.

decisions.choice: the closing speaks of the readers in the third person
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Paul's closing blessings say "with you" (Colossians 4:18; Philippians 4:23). Here he says "the brothers" and "all who love our Lord" (verse 24). This fits a letter meant to be read in more than one church; some early manuscripts lack "in Ephesus" in 1:1.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: Men and women are meant (m1); "brothers" is the traditional form.

decisions.choice: May God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ give
alternatives: Peace to the brothers and sisters
decisions.reason: Readable turns the greeting into a prayer and names the givers first.

source.text: ἡ χάρις μετὰ πάντων τῶν ἀγαπώντων τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: The grace [be] with all the [ones] loving the Lord of us Jesus Christ in incorruption.

en.L: Grace [be] with all who love our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} in incorruption.
en.B: Grace be with all who love our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} with a love that will never perish.
en.R: May God's grace be with everyone who loves our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} with a love that will never die.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: no "Amen" at the end
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "Amen", as copyists often did at the end of a book.

decisions.choice: in incorruption describes the love: a love that does not decay
alternatives: our Lord Jesus Christ, who is immortal
decisions.reason: The phrase stands at the end and could go with several words. It most likely describes how believers love Christ: with a love that lasts. It could instead go with "grace" (grace with them for immortal life) or with "our Lord Jesus Christ" (who lives in immortality).

decisions.choice: incorruption: what cannot decay or die
decisions.reason: ἀφθαρσία is the imperishable life of the age to come (Romans 2:7; 1 Corinthians 15:42, 15:53-54; 2 Timothy 1:10).

decisions.choice: the grace: God's grace, of which the letter has spoken
decisions.reason: The article points to the grace already named in the letter (1:2, 1:6-7, 2:5-8).

decisions.choice: with a love that will never perish (B); never die (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the reading chosen in m2; Literal keeps the open phrase "in incorruption".

decisions.choice: May God's grace
decisions.reason: Readable makes the closing a prayer and says whose grace it is (m4).
